title: Meshes, points and Gaussian splats
hook: What each one really stores, why a splat has no surface, and what SplatToMesh has to invent to get one.

verified.claim: SPLAT holds positions, scales, rotations, opacities and spherical-harmonic colour, each per Gaussian.
SplatToMesh builds density and colour grids, picks a level with Otsu, runs Surface Nets, drops small components, applies Taubin smoothing, then samples colour.
The renderer composites front to back across depth slabs.
The source comment on _io.py's POINT type says no core code references it, and point clouds reach core as file types and depth nodes.
The 3D Gaussian Splatting abstract describes real-time radiance field rendering.

unchecked: Our density grid in the lab uses round Gaussians. The real node uses each Gaussian's full oriented covariance.
The Hunyuan graph gives a mesh and not a splat. We have no splat model on our test machine, so no splat graph here was run, and we show no splat result of our own.
Rules of thumb on file size come from counting fields. Core also writes spz and ksplat, which its tooltip says keep the base colour only, with spz compressed and ksplat not. We did not measure them.
